chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Abi Khadeeja, who said:
We took seeds of Ajwa dates from Medina, and a companion of ours planted them in an orchard. From them grew the Sakkar, al-Heyroun, al-Shahriz, al-Sarfan, and every type of date.
ai.seo_question: What varieties of dates grew from Ajwa seeds planted in Medina?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the botanical phenomenon of grafting or natural mutation in date palms, illustrating the Prophet's tradition of agricultural excellence. It serves as a practical example of how specific cultivars like Ajwa can yield diverse varieties, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on the utility and blessing of the Prophet's homeland produce.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Hashim, from Abu Khadeeja who said,

‘We took a variety of dates from Al-Medina, so a companion of our planted it in an orchard. So there came out from it, Al-Sakkar, and Al-Heyroun, and Al-Shahreyz, and Al-Sarfan, and every type of date’.
en.sarwar: 13. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu Hashim from abu Khadijah who has said the following: “

Once we took date-stones of al-‘ Ajwah from al-Madinah and a friend of us planted them in a garden. What grew thereof was al-Sukkar, al-Hirun, al-Shahriz and al-Sarfan (names of certain kinds of dates) and all kinds of dates.’”
